title: Password Security & Management Risk Calculator
metaDescription: Assess your password security risks and get personalized recommendations to strengthen your digital defense against cyber threats.
description: Evaluate your current password practices and discover security vulnerabilities. Get a comprehensive risk assessment with actionable recommendations to improve your password security and protect your digital accounts from cyber attacks.

formula: const lengthScore = passwordLength === '1-7' ? 0 : passwordLength === '8-12' ? 25 : passwordLength === '13-16' ? 60 : 85; const complexityScore = passwordComplexity === 'simple' ? 0 : passwordComplexity === 'mixed' ? 30 : passwordComplexity === 'complex' ? 70 : 85; const reuseScore = passwordReuse === 'always' ? 0 : passwordReuse === 'often' ? 15 : passwordReuse === 'sometimes' ? 50 : 90; const managerBonus = passwordManager ? 20 : 0; const tfaScore = twoFactorAuth === 'none' ? 0 : twoFactorAuth === 'few' ? 20 : twoFactorAuth === 'some' ? 50 : 80; const accountPenalty = Math.max(0, (importantAccounts - 10) * 2); const ageScore = passwordAge === 'never' ? 0 : passwordAge === 'rarely' ? 30 : passwordAge === 'annually' ? 60 : 85; const baseScore = (lengthScore + complexityScore + reuseScore + tfaScore + ageScore) / 5; const finalScore = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, baseScore + managerBonus - accountPenalty)); const vulnerabilities = (passwordLength === '1-7' ? 1 : 0) + (passwordReuse === 'always' || passwordReuse === 'often' ? 1 : 0) + (twoFactorAuth === 'none' ? 1 : 0) + (!passwordManager ? 1 : 0); const grade = finalScore >= 90 ? 'A' : finalScore >= 80 ? 'B' : finalScore >= 70 ? 'C' : finalScore >= 60 ? 'D' : 'F'; const improvement = Math.round((100 - finalScore) * 0.8); return { riskScore: Math.round(finalScore), riskGrade: grade, vulnerabilityCount: vulnerabilities, improvementPotential: improvement };

educational.methodology: This calculator evaluates your password security based on industry best practices including NIST guidelines and cybersecurity expert recommendations. It considers password strength, uniqueness, authentication methods, and account management practices to provide a comprehensive risk assessment.
tips: Use a reputable password manager to generate and store unique passwords for every account
Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) on all accounts that support it, especially banking and email
Create passwords with at least 12-16 characters using a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols
Consider using passphrases with random words for better security and memorability
Never reuse passwords across multiple accounts, especially important ones
Use Incognito Browser for secure browsing to protect your login sessions
Regularly update passwords for critical accounts and after any security breaches
Avoid using personal information like birthdays, names, or common words in passwords
